name: Purpose-bounded reading width
summary: Bound line length/readable content width when the principal task is reading while permitting wider compositions for data-heavy or multi-region work.
problem: Unbounded measure in long text can hinder line tracking, but overly narrow widths can impede dense task workflows.
context: Editorial, explanatory, documentation and service-form content rather than full-width analytic workbenches.
observed_solution: Use context-appropriate constrained reading areas, with deliberate supporting columns where useful, not an arbitrary universal fixed width.
rationale: GOV.UK recommends service reading width around 75 characters (O12,O13); Primer gives around 80-character guideline (O23); Carbon identifies editorial, product/docs and high-density layout models (O18,O20).
tradeoffs: Dense tables, canvases and dashboards may benefit from full available width.
Different languages, fonts and zoom settings change measured line length.
applicability: Long-form readable main content, service instructions or documentation.
non_applicability: Large data tables, GIS maps, high-density multi-panel professional tools requiring horizontal information.
accessibility_implications: WCAG Reflow constrains narrow/zoomed layouts, but does not specify 75- or 80-character limits.
responsive_implications: Width should adapt without unnecessary two-dimensional scrolling under applicable WCAG exceptions.
implementation_notes: Treat GOV.UK 1020px and Primer PageLayout CSS widths as distinct system implementations.
Preserve source-dependent dimensions, not universal numbers.

counterexamples.summary: IBM Carbon explicitly describes full-width high-density interface models as fit for some task-heavy products.
counterexamples.context: Catalogs, dashboards, data visualization and dense workbenches.

version_context: GOV.UK/Primer unpinned docs; Carbon indexed official pages updated Sep 25 2026; WCAG 2.2 (2024)
